text: This is one of the most common real interview questions in T-SQL. Every table that needs an auto-generated key uses an IDENTITY column — but reading that generated value back safely takes knowing the difference between three very similar-looking functions.

DemoID int identity one comma one, not null, primary key. Identity one comma one means start at 1, and go up by 1 on every successful insert. You never include DemoID in the insert yourself — SQL Server generates it automatically.

Select scope underscore identity as NewDemoID. SCOPE_IDENTITY returns the last identity value inserted by your current session, in your current scope — meaning the statement you're actually running. This is the function you should reach for by default.

At underscore underscore IDENTITY looks similar, but it's dangerously broader: it returns the last identity value inserted anywhere in the current session — even inside a trigger that fired because of your insert. If that trigger inserts into a different table, at-identity silently returns the trigger's value instead of yours.

IDENT underscore CURRENT of LessonDemo returns the last identity value generated for that specific table, across any session — not just yours. With multiple users inserting concurrently, this can return a value someone else just generated. It's the least safe of the three.
Next lesson: SEQUENCE objects — a standalone number generator that isn't tied to one table or column at all.
